result.impl:
I implemented `test_run_failed`, the sixth zero-config send-back, and committed it in the worktree. The spec's tests and checks pass: 131 tests in the requested suite, mypy clean, ruff clean on the files I touched. All 11 guards were caught by mutation testing. The offline replay fired it 0 times, and no other finding changed. One thing to know first: this build is ahead of the decision document's own gate, and the spec leaves out one guard the reviewers asked for (both under "Before merging").

**Where it is**
- Worktree: `/home/user/Vacant/.claude/worktrees/wf_47b337c8-2fc-1`
- Branch: `worktree-wf_47b337c8-2fc-1`
- Commit: `ef9b52bb539868bb0f56a2eb713af5d65a4d5c9c`, Chinese message with both attribution lines.
- Base: the worktree was created at `main` (a725be78), which has no `vacant_network/trace/`. I reset the branch to `claude/vacant-verification-redesign-jv7eou` @ 9d605b90, the branch the main checkout is on, before starting.

**Files changed**
- `vacant_network/trace/evidence.py`: the new check and its `finding_id` key (one per request, so a second failure shows as "still open").
- `vacant_network/trace/review.py`: the send-back line, checked for KS-1 when the module loads.
- `vacant_network/trace/zerostop.py`: the delivery-note line, the note-only cases under "Not verified", a line in "What was checked" giving the test/build run count and the last run's outcome, and a screen summary.
- `tests/test_zero_testrun.py`: new, 38 tests.

**How it behaves**
- **What counts as a test run:** only commands where the runner actually runs. Wrappers are stripped first (`VAR=`, `env`, `timeout N`, `uv run`, `npx`, `.venv/bin/`). `pip install pytest`, `which pytest`, `grep pytest` and `cat pytest.ini` don't count. I added this because the plain `RUNNERS` search would treat a failed `pip install pytest` as a failed test run. No benchmark-specific scripts were added.
- **How failure is decided:** from the recorded error only, never the output text. Only the error's first line is read (Claude's `Exit code N`). An interrupted run counts as unknown, and so does a run with no end record.
- **Which agents it covers:** only Claude Code and pi report errors, so it never fires on Codex or OpenCode.
- **When it only goes in the note:** code changed after the failure, the workspace wasn't fully observed afterwards, the final message is missing, mentions a failure, or ends with a question.
- **No double send-back:** it is skipped when the existing "tests pass" claim check already sent back the same step.
- **Byte-identical:** a clean run sends nothing; in test (i) every hook response matches a run without Vacant installed.

**Tests**
- Spec cases (a)–(i) are covered, plus: no double send-back, the two-round limit, unknown and interrupted runs, missing final message, unobserved changes, sent-back-then-disclosed, cut-off runs, observe mode, and the last-turn budget case.
- The requested command gives 131 passed. The broader `test_trace_*`, `test_adapters_*` and `test_zero_mode` files also pass (205).
- mypy (CI scope): no issues.
- ruff (CI selection) on `vacant_network`, `examples`, `tests`: clean. On the full CI scope it reports 27 errors, all in two older archived scripts under `ops/eval/evidence_20260926_local/` that I didn't touch, so CI will stay red on ruff until those are fixed or excluded.

**Mutation check: 11 of 11 guards caught** (each removed alone makes at least one test fail)

| Guard removed | Test that fails |
|---|---|
| exit status only (output text also counts) | f |
| code changed afterwards | d |
| final message mentions failure | b, b2 |
| final message ends with a question | c |
| no double send-back with the "tests pass" claim check | j, j2 |
| runner must be the command itself | g (5 cases) |
| run with no end record | l |

**Offline replay (formal_v3, all 6 C-arm cells, 474 chains, no model, no docker)**
- Each chain was copied to a temp dir first. I ran the evidence check three ways: no final message, the real final message from pi's session file, and a synthetic "Done." (1,422 runs), with both the committed code and a `git archive` of HEAD.
- `test_run_failed` fired 0 times and was never added as a note. The pi sessions had 2,821 bash calls and none ran a test command, which is also why 0 is expected rather than informative.
- Other findings were identical in all 1,422 runs (132/125/132 per final-message variant, old and new). Full results matched except in one chain (`g12-off-C2-58-s1`). There, the old code alone gives different "traced" and "derived" counts from process to process: 147/23 with `PYTHONHASHSEED=1`, 156/14 with `=2`. Old and new match exactly when the seed is fixed. The cause is `Evidence.corpus()` looping over a set. It is an existing randomness bug that I left alone.
- Outputs: `scratchpad/testrun/{old_all,new_merged}.jsonl`, scripts `replay.py`, `compare.py`, `mutate.py`.

**Before merging**
- **The decision's own gate isn't met.** DECISION_20260926_BIGGER_EFFECT_REVIEW §六.1 says to build candidate 2 only after replay on recorded traces with test runs: R530 SOLO accuracy ≥ 0.8, and 0 false send-backs on turns where the agent asks the person something. The DABstep replay can't show either, and the interactive replay hasn't been done.
- **The spec leaves out a guard the reviewers asked for.** Send back only if the same command passed earlier in the request, otherwise note only. Without it, failures that were already there (a repo-wide `npm run lint`, for example) and requests to write a failing test that reproduces a bug will each get one send-back. The wording lets the agent answer by saying the failure is expected.
- **Known misses (never a false send-back):** `pytest | tail` and `pytest; echo …` hide the exit status, and pi errors always show as "non-zero".
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md still says there are only five kinds of send-back. I didn't edit CLAUDE.md, so that line needs your update.

findings.title: Commands that only mention a runner are counted as test runs: `|`, `;` and newlines are split even inside quotes and heredocs, so a grep with no match gets sent back as a failed test run
findings.scenario: _runs_runner splits the command on `_SEGMENT` (&&, ||, ;, |, \n) without looking at quotes or heredocs. Each fragment is then matched with RUNNERS.match, so `grep -E "jest|vitest|mocha" package.json`, `grep -rn "pytest\|unittest" tests/`, `rg "pytest|tox" pyproject.toml` and `sed -i "s|pytest|python -m pytest|" Makefile` all count as runner runs. So do a README heredoc with a `    pytest -q` line and a `git commit -m` body with a line starting `make test` or `pytest` (all confirmed with _runs_runner). Reproduced through hook.handle("claude"). The person asks "Which test runner does this project use? Don't change anything." The agent runs `grep -E "jest|vitest|mocha" package.json`, which exits 1 because nothing matched, and answers "This project has no JavaScript test runner configured". Stop returns decision=block with "Step 1 ran `grep -E \"jest|vitest|mocha\" package.json` and it ended with a failure (exit status 1)... Fix what fails and run it again". A no-match grep is sent back as a failed test run, and the agent is pushed toward adding a test framework the person never asked for. When code is written after such a grep, the delivery note tells the person "The last test or build run, step N (grep ...), failed". When such a fragment exits 0 (heredoc, sed, a commit), it becomes the "last run" with status ok. That hides a real earlier failure, and the note says "the last one did not fail" about a command that ran no tests. `failed_step` already excludes no-match searches with `_no_match_only`; this path has no such guard.
findings.fix: Tokenise with shlex (fall back to 'not a runner' when parsing fails). Split into segments only at unquoted operators, drop heredoc bodies before splitting, and count a segment only when its first token after the wrappers is the runner. As a backstop, treat any segment whose first word is grep/rg/ag/sed/awk/echo/cat/git as not a runner.

findings.title: Non-zero exits that are not test failures are sent back as failures: timeouts, pytest exit 5 (no tests collected), npm's default `exit 1` test script, and every pi timeout
findings.scenario: _run_status treats any error without NOT_A_RUN as ('failed', code). All of these were reproduced as decision=block with "Fix what fails and run it again": (1) `timeout 60 pytest -q` → Claude "Exit code 124", sent back as "exit status 124". The implementation strips `timeout N` in `_LEAD` so that it recognises the runner, then reads the wrapper's 124 as a test failure. (2) The Claude Bash tool's own timeout error "Command timed out after 2m 0.0s" → sent back as "non-zero". (3) `pytest -q -k slugify` → Exit code 5 (no tests collected) after adding a new helper; sent back as "exit status 5". (4) `npm test` in a project with npm-init's default script `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, after adding a route, with final message "This project has no test suite set up"; sent back as "exit status 1". (5) pi: the Vacant pi extension forwards only `is_error: true`, so error="tool reported an error" in every case. pi's bash tool (dist/core/tools/bash.js:256-270) raises "Command timed out after N seconds", "Command aborted" and "Command terminated without an exit code" through the same isError path, so NOT_A_RUN can never match for pi and every pi timeout counts as a failed run. None of these is a runner that finished and failed. The spec says unknown exit status ⇒ do not fire. Telling the agent to "fix what fails" when nothing failed invites unwanted edits: skipping slow tests, rewriting package.json's test script, or adding tests to make pytest collect something.
findings.fix: Treat the following as 'unknown' (note only): exit codes 124/137/143 and other codes ≥128; error or output status lines saying 'timed out', 'terminated without an exit code' or 'aborted'; pytest code 5. For pi, read only the tool output's final appended status line (`Command exited with code N` / `Command timed out…` / `Command aborted`) to get the code or classify the run as unknown. This decides whether not to fire, not whether a run failed, so it stays within 'no FAIL_OUT matching'. Optionally treat npm's literal default test script as not a run.

verdict.evidence:
The finding is real. I reproduced it through the real `hook.handle` path on the worktree commit ef9b52bb. The test is /tmp/claude-0/cand2_verify/test_nonfailure_exits.py, run with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree> /home/user/Vacant/.venv/bin/python -m pytest ... -s`. All 9 tests pass, and every case asserts that a send-back happened.

**Cause** (`vacant_network/trace/evidence.py`, `_run_status`): it reads only the first line of `s.error`. It returns "unknown" only when `NOT_A_RUN` (`interrupt|cancel+ed|abort`) matches. Any other non-empty error, or a code other than 0, is treated as `("failed", code)`.

**Cases that were sent back.** Each gave Claude `decision=block` or pi `action=continue` with "Fix what fails and run it again".
1. Claude runs `timeout 60 pytest -q` and gets `Exit code 124`. It is sent back as "exit status 124". `_LEAD` strips `timeout N` so the runner is recognised, but the 124 is the timeout's own exit code, not pytest's.
2. Claude runs `pytest -q` and gets `Command timed out after 2m 0.0s`. It is sent back as "exit status non-zero", because `NOT_A_RUN` has no pattern for "timed out". I did not check the exact wording of Claude Code's timeout message. Any timeout text that lacks interrupt, cancel or abort would be classified the same way.
3. After adding `slugify`, `pytest -q -k slugify` gets `Exit code 5` (no tests collected). It is sent back as "exit status 5".
4. `npm test`, where package.json has npm-init's default script `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, gets `Exit code 1`. The final message was "This project has no test suite set up." `MENTIONS_FAILURE` does not match that sentence, so it is sent back as "exit status 1".
5. pi reports `is_error=True` with output ending "Command timed out after 60 seconds". It is sent back as "non-zero". On pi, `capture._output_and_error` turns the error into "tool reported an error". The Vacant pi extension (`adapters/agents.py`, around line 372) forwards only `is_error: !!event.isError`.
6. pi runs that end "Command aborted" or "Command terminated without an exit code" are also sent back.

For cases 5 and 6, I read pi's own `dist/core/tools/bash.js` (lines 252-270 in the local node_modules copy). It raises timeouts, aborts and missing exit codes through the same isError path as real failures. So on pi, `NOT_A_RUN` can never match, and every pi timeout or abort counts as a failed run.

**Controls.**
- A real pytest failure (`Exit code 1`) is still sent back.
- `timeout 60 sleep 100` with `Exit code 124` is not sent back as `test_run_failed`, so the send-backs above are not a harness artifact.

**Weight of each case.** Cases 1, 2, 5 and 6 plainly break the spec's rule "if the exit status is unknown, do not fire": the runner's own result is unknown there. Cases 3 and 4 are real non-zero exits, so the spec's wording technically allows them. Even so, "fix what fails" is the wrong instruction for a run where nothing failed.

findings.title: A failure the agent did disclose is not recognised, so the agent gets up to two send-backs for something it already reported
findings.scenario:
Condition 4 reuses MENTIONS_FAILURE and checks only the last message. Reproduced as a send-back (action=continue) for each of these: (a) Chinese, the language this project's own users write in: "完成。parse() 已修改；tests/test_calc.py 的 test_float 還是沒過，是這次修改之前就有的問題，我沒有動它。" MENTIONS_FAILURE has only 失敗/錯誤, not 沒過/未通過/不通過. findings.scenario:
